title: Grateful Dead Live at Academy of Music on 1972-03-25
lineage: Dat (Sony D8) -> Samplitude Professional v11.2.1 -> FLAC/
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Apogee AD500 -> Dat (48k)

ai_review.summary: Outstanding soundboard capture of a high‑energy two‑set show packed with rare covers and monster jams like the 22‑minute Lovelight.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised as crystal‑clear and “outstanding” – a true soundboard source that lets listeners hear every nuance.  Musically the night is legendary: one‑off covers (How Sweet It Is, Are You Lonely For Me), blistering Pigpen leads, soaring vocals from Donna Jean, and marathon jams such as Playin’ and a 22‑minute Lovelight make it a must‑hear performance.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviews overwhelmingly praise both the show (unique covers, high energy, long jams) and the recording quality (outstanding soundboard). A few low‑star comments note unusual set flow, but they do not outweigh the strong positive consensus.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with no reported dropouts or muddiness; reviewers describe it as “outstanding quality.”

standout_songs: Are You Lonely For Me (Fredie King cover)
Next Time You See Me (Pigpen lead)
Beat It On Down the Line
show_quality.setlist_flow: Two sets heavy on rare covers and improvisation; the first set feels spontaneously assembled, while the second builds into extended jams and a monumental Lovelight finale.

band_member_comments.Bob: Intense rhythm‑guitar work on Lovelight compensates for his reduced vocal presence that night.
